title: Dooars on a budget: safaris and forests for less
meta_description: How to do the Dooars for ₹1,800–3,000 a day: trains instead of cars, forest lodges, shared safari jeeps, watchtowers, thalis and the weeks to avoid.
summary: The Dooars can cost ₹1,800–3,000 a day per person if you ride the trains, sleep in government forest and tourism lodges, share safari jeeps six to a vehicle and eat at roadside hotels. The two things that break budgets are reserved cars and holiday weeks. Here is how to avoid both.

sections.heading: Where the money actually goes
paras: A Dooars trip has four big costs: getting from Siliguri or Kolkata to the parks, moving between parks, safaris and rooms. Food is cheap here, and entry fees are small. The single largest line on most bills is the reserved car. A car from Siliguri to Lataguri, two days of sightseeing, a transfer to Madarihat and a drop back can easily cost ₹14,000–18,000 before anyone has eaten. For a family of five that is fine. For a couple it is the whole budget.

The second big cost is timing. Lataguri and Madarihat rooms that cost ₹2,000 on a Tuesday in February can cost ₹4,000–5,000 in Puja week or between 24 December and 1 January, and safari seats in those weeks vanish within hours of release. Here is what a frugal day and a comfortable day look like per person, sharing a room. These are indicative 2026 ranges.

sections.heading: Take the train into the Dooars
paras: The railway from NJP to Alipurduar runs straight through the Dooars, with stations at New Mal Junction (for Lataguri, 10 km), Chalsa (for Murti and Chapramari), Banarhat, Binnaguri, Madarihat and Hasimara (for Jaldapara and Chilapata), and Alipurduar (for Buxa and Jayanti). The Kanchankanya Express from Sealdah runs overnight along this line, so Kolkata travellers can wake up in the forest and save a night's hotel at the same time. Sleeper fares are about ₹400–550, indicative 2026.

From NJP, local and express trains cover the same line several times a day, taking about 2 hours to New Mal and 3–4 hours to Hasimara. Fares are tiny compared with a car. At the station, autos run to Lataguri, Murti and Madarihat for ₹150–400. Buses and shared vehicles also run along the highway from Siliguri to Lataguri for ₹100–200 a seat and on to Madarihat for a little more. Timetables and fares change, so check current status before you travel.

A car does make sense in two cases: a family of four or more, where the per-head cost drops sharply, or a trip that links Lataguri with Jhalong, Samsing or Bindu, where public transport is thin. Even then, use the train for the long legs and hire a car locally for one day.

sections.heading: Sleep in forest and tourism lodges
paras: The West Bengal government runs some of the best-placed lodges in the Dooars, and they are often the cheapest decent rooms near the parks. Murti Banani, on the bank of the Murti river, has tents from about ₹1,500 a night and rooms and cottages above that. WBTDC's Aranya Tourism Property at Madarihat sits near the Jaldapara gate. The Malangi lodge near Hasimara is a good base for Chilapata and Jaldapara. In Siliguri, WBTDC's Mainak Tourism Property is a sensible budget stop before an early train.

Government lodges book out early for weekends and holidays, so reserve on the official booking sites as soon as your dates are firm. Meals are fixed and simple, often around ₹500 a day per person, and served at set times. At Lataguri, family-run lodges and small hotels start at about ₹1,200–2,500 a room, and you can walk to the safari counter. For Buxa and Jayanti, village homestays with meals cost about ₹1,500–3,000 per person a night, indicative 2026.
list: Book government lodges as soon as booking opens for your dates; weekend rooms go first.
Ask for a room facing the forest or river; at most lodges the price is the same.
Carry cash: some forest lodges and village homestays do not take cards or UPI reliably.

sections.heading: Safaris: share the jeep, sit in a watchtower
paras: Safari jeeps are priced per vehicle, not per person, and each takes up to six. A Gorumara jeep with a watchtower costs about ₹2,500–3,500 and a Jaldapara jeep about ₹2,800–4,000, indicative 2026. Two people in a jeep pay half of that each. Six people pay a sixth. Ask your lodge or the counter at Lataguri or Madarihat to put you with other travellers; it is normal practice and the staff are used to it.

Gorumara's watchtowers are the best value in the Dooars. Jatraprasad, the Rhino Observation Point, Chukchuki, Chandrachur and Medla overlook salt licks or grassland, and you sit for about an hour as animals come to you. The tower ticket itself costs ₹70–250 per person; you pay separately for the jeep. One good watchtower session often shows more than a long drive.

Book through the forest department's official online system or at the park counter, with photo ID for every traveller that matches the ticket. Never buy from a stranger at the gate offering seats at double the price. Gorumara safaris are usually closed on Thursdays, and both parks shut from mid-June to mid-September; check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Eat where the drivers eat
paras: Roadside hotels at Lataguri, Malbazar, Chalsa and Madarihat serve rice, dal, a vegetable, fish or egg curry and chutney for ₹100–200, indicative 2026. Fish from the Teesta and local rivers turns up often. Tea is the local CTC, strong and milky, at ₹10–20 a cup. Resort restaurants charge three or four times as much for the same food, so eat lunch outside even if dinner is at your lodge.

Lodge dinners are often included or fixed-price, so check before you book a room-only rate that looks cheaper. Carry snacks and water on safari days and transfer days, because shops are few on forest roads.

sections.heading: Pick the right weeks
paras: The cheapest good weeks are mid-November to mid-December, mid-January to early March, and mid-week in April. The parks are open, the weather is dry, and lodges often charge 20–40% less mid-week than at weekends. October after Puja is also good value. Avoid Puja week, the Christmas and New Year week, and long weekends, when rates double and safari seats sell out.

From mid-June to mid-September the parks are closed. Rooms are at their cheapest and the forests are green, but you came for the animals, so this is a poor trade unless you just want quiet lodges and rain.

sections.heading: A frugal three-night plan
paras: Here is how we would spend three nights in the Dooars on about ₹7,000–9,000 per person, sharing a room, not counting the train from home. Arrive at Chalsa on the overnight Kanchankanya Express or a morning train from NJP and take an auto to Murti, ₹150–300. Sleep in a Murti Banani tent and spend the afternoon by the river, with a watchtower slot at Chandrachur or Medla if one is free.

Next morning, ride an auto to Lataguri, check into a family lodge and take an afternoon Gorumara watchtower safari in a shared jeep. On day three, take a bus or train east to Madarihat, check into a simple hotel near the gate and book the dawn Jaldapara safari for the following morning. After breakfast on day four, an auto to Hasimara station gets you on a train home. You will have seen two national parks, a river and a hundred kilometres of tea gardens without hiring a single car. Check current status before you travel, as train halts and safari timings change.

sections.heading: What to skip
paras: A few things cost money without making the trip better. We would rather you spent it on a second safari.
list: Package sightseeing that stacks five places in one day; you spend it in the car.
Elephant rides at premium prices from unlicensed operators; ride only where the forest department runs them.
Reserved airport cars for a couple; a shared auto to Siliguri and a bus or train onward costs a fraction.
Resort lunches on safari days; eat at a roadside hotel.
Gift shops selling 'Dooars tea' in fancy tins; buy loose CTC from a local shop instead.

faqs.q: How much does a Dooars trip cost per day
faqs.a: On a frugal plan, about ₹1,800–3,000 per person a day, sharing a room, using trains and buses, staying in forest lodges or family lodges and sharing safari jeeps, indicative 2026. A comfortable trip with a private car and a mid-range resort runs about ₹5,000–8,000 a day per person. Holiday weeks cost noticeably more.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to reach Lataguri from Siliguri
faqs.a: Take a bus or shared vehicle from Siliguri along the highway via Sevoke and Malbazar, about 2–2.5 hours, for ₹100–200 a seat, indicative 2026. A local train to New Mal Junction plus an auto for the last 10 km also works and costs about the same. A reserved car costs about ₹2,800–3,800.

faqs.q: How can I save money on a Gorumara safari
faqs.a: Fill the jeep. Safaris are priced per vehicle for up to six, so sharing with other travellers cuts your cost to a sixth. Choose a watchtower slot rather than a longer drive, go mid-week, and book on the official forest department system rather than through middlemen. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Are government lodges in the Dooars good value
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Murti Banani, Aranya at Madarihat and the Malangi lodge near Hasimara sit close to the forests at prices well below private resorts. Rooms are simple and meals fixed, and maintenance varies from lodge to lodge. Book early on the official sites, as weekend rooms go fast.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to visit the Dooars in the monsoon
faqs.a: Rooms are cheapest from June to August, but Gorumara, Jaldapara and the other parks are closed from mid-June to mid-September, so there are no safaris. You can still enjoy rivers, tea gardens and quiet lodges. For wildlife, the cheapest good months are November, February and early March, mid-week.

faqs.q: Can I visit the Dooars without a car
faqs.a: Yes. Trains connect New Mal, Chalsa, Madarihat, Hasimara and Alipurduar; autos link stations with Lataguri, Murti and Madarihat; and buses run along the highway. Safaris use licensed jeeps, so you never need your own vehicle inside the parks. Transfers are slower, so finish them before dark.

faqs.q: Which month is cheapest for the Dooars with safaris
faqs.a: Late January, February and early March, mid-week, are the best balance: parks open, dry weather and lodges discounting by 20–40% outside weekends. Late November and early December are also good. Avoid Puja week and 24 December to 1 January, when prices are highest.

faqs.q: How much should I budget for food in the Dooars
faqs.a: About ₹300–500 a day if you eat at roadside hotels, where a thali with fish or egg curry costs ₹100–200, indicative 2026. Lodge meals at government properties often cost around ₹500 a day per person. Resort restaurants charge much more. Carry snacks for safari days.

faqs.q: Is a budget Dooars trip good for families
faqs.a: Yes. Families can use the overnight train from Kolkata, stay at Murti Banani or a Lataguri family lodge, and share a safari jeep with another family to fill six seats. For four or more people, a car for one or two days can cost the same per head as public transport and saves effort.
